newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanians support anti-Israel protest, organisers.
newsitem.headline: Jordanians support anti-Israel protest, organisers.

text.p: Thousands of Jordanians supported a symbolic strike to protest against the holding of the first Israeli trade fair in the kingdom, organisers said on Thursday.

"Thousands phoned us declaring their support of the action," Ali Abu-Sukar, the head of the "anti-(Israeli) normalisation committee" in the Islamist-dominated 37,000 strong-member Engineers Union, told Reuters.
There was no independent confirmation of how many Jordanians heeded the call for the one-hour stoppage on Thursday.

Ali said campaigners against the fair had retreated from an earlier three-day stoppage call after "our aims were met." Over 1,000 Jordanians ended their protest outside the fair at the end of Wednesday's first day of the exhibition.
The protest was organised by a "national committee" that represents a broad coalition of 21 parties, 18 unions and business lobbies.

The campaign reflects anti-Israeli feelings among many Jordanians who still shun contacts despite a 1994 peace treaty that ended a 46-year state of war with Israel. It has been the largest public protest against Israel since the peace treaty.
Abu-Sukar said organisers also called for Friday prayers outside the site of the fair, which is heavily protected by police forces to prevent any disruption by demonstrators.

Officials privately say the anti-Israeli lobby has failed to enlist the support of a majority of Jordanians in a highly- publicised campaign to prove a sweeping popular rejection of normal ties with Israel.
"Our heroic Jordanian people, you were great yesterday and will remain," said a campaign slogan published in all the front pages of the country's newspapers.
Seventy Israeli companies and over 200 Israeli businessmen are taking part in the event.
